- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.16) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +1.5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots downward; cap forecast decline to 10-15% below peak or align with 20-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.27) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates upside; cap forecast growth to 1.5x recent 10-day average or use sentiment as decay-weighted multiplier.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.2x recent 30-day average, reduce by 10-20% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward momentum in bearish sentiment; add 0.5–1.0% buffer below forecast if sentiment < -0.10 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.16+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted median of last 5 days.
